claim: SPIE 2021 paper states optical metrology has limited resolution for 3D NAND, especially toward the bottom of HAR structures; it proposes in-line CD-SAXS for CD, ellipticity and tilt profiles through the whole channel hole
document: Fan M., Ranjit R., Thurber A. et al., 'High resolution profiles of 3D NAND pillars using x-ray scattering metrology', Proc. SPIE 11611, 116110S (2021) - abstract on SPIE proceedings volume page
quote: Optical metrology can monitor CDs of device structures, but has limited resolution for 3D NAND, especially towards the bottom of high aspect ratio (HAR) structures
note: Abstract only; full text not retrieved (SPIE Digital Library bot challenge). Affiliations not shown on the volume page; abstract presents a 'production-ready CD-SAXS system', so vendor authorship is possible (unverified). Cited by IRDS 2024 Metrology ref [174]. DOI 10.1117/12.2585217.

claim: Samsung (Flash Process Development) + Nova paper: the main HAR challenge for lateral parameters in multi-deck 3D NAND is their variation with feature depth (the profile)
document: Yoon J., Park J., Shin M., Ihm D. (Samsung R&D Center, Flash Process Development) + Bismuth O., Ferber S., Ofek J., Turovets I., Kim I. (Nova), 'Unique Spectral Interferometry solutions for complex High Aspect Ratio 3D NAND structures', Proc. SPIE 12955, 129551S (2024)
quote: Currently, the main challenges for High Aspect Ratio (HAR) lateral parameters are the profiles or variations of the lateral parameters with the feature depth
note: Chipmaker + vendor co-authored (Nova part vendor-authored). Volume publication date 29 Apr 2024 per SPIE volume page; file name date = conference week. Same paper p.2: nonperiodic staircase contacts are 'a challenge for traditional scatterometry, which usually measures repetitive grating structures'.

claim: Same Samsung+Nova paper: bottom CD of HAR through-cell metal contacts measured with spectral interferometry (VTS) plus an ML model trained on reference CDs along the profile; correlation to reference R2 = 0.89, RMSE below 5 Å; repeatability 3-sigma 0.15% after spot-location optimisation (target smaller than spot)
document: Yoon J., Park J., Shin M., Ihm D. (Samsung R&D Center, Flash Process Development) + Bismuth O., Ferber S., Ofek J., Turovets I., Kim I. (Nova), 'Unique Spectral Interferometry solutions for complex High Aspect Ratio 3D NAND structures', Proc. SPIE 12955, 129551S (2024)
quote: The correlation plot shows a good R2=0.89 and a small RMSE (Root Mean Square Error) below 5A
note: ML ('AI') solution rather than a physical optical model; reference metrology type is not named in the paper. p.6: target area 'smaller than the measurement spot size'; repeatability 'down to 3sigma of 0.15%'. Chipmaker + Nova co-authored.

claim: Same paper: on a 3-deck cell-over-periphery stack, CMP removal rate in the cell array was 1.5-2x that on the dedicated OCD target, so scribe/proxy OCD targets misrepresent the array; authors state in-cell measurement is required
document: Yoon J., Park J., Shin M., Ihm D. (Samsung R&D Center, Flash Process Development) + Bismuth O., Ferber S., Ofek J., Turovets I., Kim I. (Nova), 'Unique Spectral Interferometry solutions for complex High Aspect Ratio 3D NAND structures', Proc. SPIE 12955, 129551S (2024)
quote: the removal rate in the Cell sites is 1.5 to 2 times higher than on the OCD target
note: p.5 also: 'Measurements in the Cell are a must for the process control of this 3-deck application.' Chipmaker + Nova co-authored.

claim: Nova review paper claims its vertical travelling scatterometry (scatterometry + spectral interferometry) enabled full Z-direction profiling of deep 3D NAND structures, which it says was previously inaccessible with OCD alone
document: Turovets I. (Nova), 'The art of holistic metrology (in memory of Alok Vaid)', Proc. SPIE 13981, 1398104 (2026); manuscript posted by Nova
quote: enabled complete Z-direction profiling of deep 3D structures, such as 3D NAND, something previously inaccessible with OCD alone
note: Vendor-authored review with no new data; capability claim about Nova's own technique, hence [C]. Supporting data in TH-003 (Samsung+Nova). Article number 1398104 / DOI 10.1117/12.3100570 from the SPIE 13981 volume page.

claim: Mid-IR CD paper: common amorphous-carbon hardmasks for advanced 3D NAND are opaque in the traditional OCD (UV-VIS-NIR) range; mid-IR ellipsometric CD gives channel-hole z-profiles and hardmask bottom CD
document: Antonelli G.A., Keller N., Ribaudo T. et al., 'Ellipsometric critical dimension metrology employing mid-infrared wavelengths for high-aspect-ratio channel hole module etch processes', Proc. SPIE 11611, 116111O (2021) - abstract on SPIE proceedings volume page
quote: the most common amorphous carbon hardmask materials for advanced 3D NAND nodes are opaque in the traditional OCD wavelength range
note: Abstract only; affiliations not shown; abstract describes an IRCD 'platform suitable for fab production' (vendor authorship possible, unverified). Cited as ref 16 by IBM+Nova JM3 2023 (TH-015). DOI 10.1117/12.2583786.

claim: SPIE 2024 paper: 3D flash memory-hole CDs are typically measured by RCWA-based optical metrology that needs costly, destructive SEM/TEM reference; it uses CD-SAXS as the non-destructive ground-truth reference to train an optical-CD (ML) hole-profile solution
document: Chouaib H., Shi T., Chou A. et al., 'Leveraging x-ray scatterometry and machine learning to enable robust and high-throughput optical critical dimension metrology for advanced 3D flash memory contact hole profile', Proc. SPIE 12955, 129553F (2024) - abstract on SPIE proceedings volume page
quote: we utilize critical dimension smallangle x-ray scatterometry (CD-SAXS) that provides reliable and nondestructive ground truth reference
note: Abstract only (full text not retrieved); affiliations not shown (vendor authorship possible, unverified). Same abstract: '(RCWA) based optical metrology that requires costly and destructive scanning electron microscopy (SEM) or transmission electron microscopy (TEM) reference'. DOI 10.1117/12.3010992.

claim: SPIE 2026 paper: for 3D NAND channel-hole profiles, CD-SAXS and OCD each have strengths and limits tied to spot size and model dependence
document: Choi D., Jang Y., Seo S. et al., 'High-resolution 3D NAND profile measurement using optical metrology and machine learning', Proc. SPIE 13981, 1398126 (2026) - abstract on SPIE proceedings volume page
page_or_section: Volume 13981 page, session '3D Profile and High Aspect Ratio Metrology', abstract of 1398126
quote: critical dimension small-angle X-ray scattering (CD-SAXS) and optical CD (OCD) each have strengths and limitations related to spot size and model dependencies
note: Abstract only; full text and affiliations not retrieved (SPIE Digital Library and spie.org paper page returned bot-challenge stubs). Matches the lead from the earlier chat. Same authors (Jang, Choi) on the CD-SAXS within-spot paper TH-011. DOI 10.1117/12.3090491.

claim: Same paper: hybrid metrology trains physics-informed ML on CD-SAXS-derived CDs plus spectroscopic-ellipsometer spectra; against SEM reference all sites R2 > 0.95, average slope 0.899, best slope 0.989 at R2 0.982
value: R2 >0.95 (all sites); avg slope 0.899; best slope 0.989 (R2 0.982)
document: Choi D., Jang Y., Seo S. et al., Proc. SPIE 13981, 1398126 (2026) - abstract on SPIE proceedings volume page
quote: with all sites achieving R 2 > 0.95, an average slope of 0.899, and a best-case slope of 0.989 with R 2 of 0.982
note: Abstract only; number of sites/wafers not stated in the abstract. 'R 2' = R-squared (superscript split in page text). Verifies the earlier-chat lead (R2>0.95 vs SEM).

claim: Same paper: the role left to optical CD is local measurement - the small optical spot gives localized CD-profile measurement and better control in edge regions, with CD-SAXS supplying the CD labels
document: Choi D., Jang Y., Seo S. et al., Proc. SPIE 13981, 1398126 (2026) - abstract on SPIE proceedings volume page
quote: This approach enables localized CD profile measurement with small optical spot sizes, improving process control in edge regions
note: Abstract only. Compare the ~300 µm CD-SAXS spot in the same group's 2025 paper (TH-011).

claim: SPIE 2025 paper (same author group): CD-SAXS signals on 3D NAND HARC mask holes were related to hole-to-hole variation (CD, tilt, depth, pitch) inside the ~300 µm CD-SAXS spot, using mass CD-SEM and 3D tomography as references
document: Jang Y., Choi D., Song J.K. et al., 'A study of CD-SAXS within-spot uniformity with mass CDSEM and 3D tomography', Proc. SPIE 13426, 134263I (2025) - abstract on SPIE proceedings volume page
quote: within 300μm spot of CD-SAXS
note: Abstract only; affiliations not retrieved. Spot size limits what CD-SAXS can resolve locally (edges, within-array variation); see TH-010. DOI 10.1117/12.3048889.

claim: IRDS Metrology roadmap: very tall 3D NAND and DRAM structures scatter much more strongly, so CD-SAXS already has the throughput for HAR contact holes and commercial in-line CD-SAXS tools have entered fabs
document: IEEE International Roadmap for Devices and Systems (IRDS) 2024 Edition, Metrology chapter
quote: CD-SAXS has the required throughput for characterization of HAR contact holes and commercially available in-line tools have recently been introduced to the fab
note: Industry roadmap (IEEE IRDS), not a peer-reviewed paper. Identical sentence in the 2022 Edition and 2023 Update Metrology chapters (both saved: 2022-12-31_ieee-irds_IRDS-2022-metrology-chapter.pdf, 2023-12-31_ieee-irds_IRDS-2023-metrology-chapter.pdf). p.20: HAR memory scatters 'orders of magnitude stronger than logic structures'. Release month not printed; file-name date is a placeholder.

claim: SPIE 2026 paper on Axion CD-SAXS (abstract cites a KLA simulation engine): conventional channel-hole tilt extraction needs scattering data at many angles of incidence, limiting throughput; physics-augmented AI cut AOIs from 13 to 2 and acquisition time by more than 6x
document: Lee T.J., Liman C., Li P.M. et al., 'Axion physics-augmented AI solutions for rapid, precise, and robust tilt measurement in memory devices', Proc. SPIE 13981, 139813C (2026) - abstract on SPIE proceedings volume page
quote: throughput is drastically improved by reducing the number of AOIs from 13 to just 2
note: Abstract only; likely vendor-authored (abstract names Axion and 'the simulation engine developed by KLA'); affiliations not shown. Same abstract: CD-SAXS 'is a widely recognized technique for structural characterization in advanced memory devices'. DOI 10.1117/12.3090205.

claim: SPIE 2021 vendor-tool paper: an in-line transmission-SAXS (XCD) solution measures shape and tilt of HAR structures such as 3D NAND channel holes and DRAM capacitors in a few minutes per site; XCD-OCD hybrid metrology named as a future opportunity
document: Wormington M., Ginsburg A., Reichental I. et al., 'X-ray critical dimension metrology solution for high aspect ratio semiconductor structures', Proc. SPIE 11611, 116110W (2021) - abstract on SPIE proceedings volume page
quote: with typical measurements taking only a few minutes per site
note: Abstract only; names the Sirius-XCD tool and NanoDiffract software (vendor products; affiliations not shown). Same abstract: 'such as 3D NAND channel holes and DRAM capacitors'; 'possibilities of XCD-OCD synergies including hybrid metrology'. Cited by IRDS 2024 ref [175] and IBM+Nova JM3 2023 ref 15. DOI 10.1117/12.2583966.

claim: IBM Research + Nova journal paper: X-ray scattering and mid-IR ellipsometry in-line tools have been demonstrated for CD metrology of 3D NAND channel holes, but further tool development is needed for patterned wafers in advanced logic
document: Schmidt D., Medikonda M., Rizzolo M., Silvestre C., Frougier J., Greene A., Breton M. (IBM Research) + Cepler A., Ofek J., Kaplan I., Koret R., Turovets I. (Nova), 'Spectral interferometry for fully integrated device metrology', J. Micro/Nanopattern. Mater. Metrol. 22(3) 031203 (2023), CC BY 4.0
quote: have been demonstrated for CD metrology in 3D NAND channel holes
note: Chipmaker research (IBM) + vendor co-authored; open access (CC BY 4.0, p.1), copy hosted by Nova. Sentence begins 'Although x-ray scattering15 and mid-infrared ellipsometry16 in-line tools'; ref 15 = Wormington 2021 (TH-014), ref 16 = Antonelli 2021 (TH-006). Logic requirements in TH-023.

claim: SPIE 2024 paper: DRAM storage-node profile during HAR etch is one of the most challenging metrology steps; conventional OCD models built from stacked cylinders cannot give an accurate model, so a polynomial 'hyper-profile' and model-guided ML (MGML) are used
document: Lee J., Mo S., Ryu S. et al., 'Non-destructive metrology techniques for measuring hole profile in DRAM storage node', Proc. SPIE 12955, 129552X (2024) - abstract on SPIE proceedings volume page
quote: Conventional 3D modeling in Optical Critical Dimension (OCD) metrology has typically used multiple cylinder stacks. This method cannot provide an accurate model
note: Abstract only; affiliations not retrieved. Same abstract: 'DRAM storage node profile measurement during high aspect ratio (HAR) etch has been one of the most challenging metrology steps'; MGML said to 'better decorrelate profile CDs'. No X-ray in this abstract. DOI 10.1117/12.3010503.

claim: SPIE 2024 paper: for HAR structures such as DRAM and VNAND the computing power needed for physical OCD modelling grows exponentially, so ML with reference data is crucial, but scarce labelled data causes overfitting; their few-shot method used 9 reference points on 3 DoE wafers
document: Kim M., Kim Q., Chang K.-B. et al., 'A few-shot machine learning-based OCD metrology algorithm with anomaly detection and wafer-level data augmentation', Proc. SPIE 12955, 129550U (2024) - abstract on SPIE proceedings volume page
quote: for high aspect ratio structures such as DRAM and VNAND, where the required computing power for physical modeling increases exponentially
note: Abstract only; affiliations not retrieved. Same abstract: 'limitation of available labeled data, which causes overfitting'; 'only 9 reference training data are used on three design of experiment (DoE) wafers'. DOI 10.1117/12.3009965.

claim: SPIE 2026 invited paper: ML-based OCD built on simulated spectra faces an ill-posed inverse problem - one spectrum can map to several structures (solution multiplicity), worse when the database spans a wider process window; shown on development-stage DRAM OCD data
document: Kim Q., Kim S., Cho W. et al., 'Optimization of optical metrology simulation domains in solving inverse problems of machine learning based OCD metrology' (invited), Proc. SPIE 13981, 139811P (2026) - abstract on SPIE proceedings volume page
quote: OCD metrology relies on an inherently ill-posed inverse problem in which a single measured spectrum can correspond to multiple possible structural solutions
note: Abstract only; affiliations not retrieved. 'Invited Paper' per proceedings.com table of contents for volume 13981 (saved: 2026-04-22_proceedings-com_toc-spie-13981.pdf). No X-ray in abstract. DOI 10.1117/12.3090163.

claim: IRDS Metrology roadmap names parameter cross-correlation when modelling complex features as the main challenge for scatterometry, plus quantum-confinement shifts in optical properties as features shrink; hybrid metrology may mitigate
document: IEEE International Roadmap for Devices and Systems (IRDS) 2024 Edition, Metrology chapter
quote: achieving successful scatterometry metrology on a given process: Parameter cross-correlations when modeling complex features
note: Industry roadmap. Same paragraph: 'quantum confinement effects may yield dimensionally dependent shifts in the optical properties'; 'multi-tool inspection using hybrid metrology may mitigate this challenge'.

claim: IRDS Metrology roadmap: for vertically stacked GAA manufacturing, scatterometry is one of the best-potential in-line solutions (non-destructive, precise, accurate, productive)
document: IEEE International Roadmap for Devices and Systems (IRDS) 2024 Edition, Metrology chapter
quote: where the scatterometry is (one of) the best-potential solutions for non-destructive, precise, accurate, and highly productive metrology
note: Industry roadmap; cites Chouaib et al., ASMC 2024 (GAA sheet-specific scatterometry) as ref [163].

claim: IRDS: most CD-SAXS demonstrations for logic used synchrotrons; lab CD-SAXS can serve as reference metrology, but in-line logic use needs much better compact X-ray sources to reach <1 min per measurement with a <100 µm spot
document: IEEE International Roadmap for Devices and Systems (IRDS) 2024 Edition, Metrology chapter
quote: Laboratory-based CD-SAXS can be used for reference metrology, but in-line metrology for logic applications will require significant improvements in compact X-ray sources
note: Industry roadmap; same text in 2022 and 2023 editions. The µ glyph of the spot size is missing in the text layer ('<100 m'). Same page: 'Most reported demonstrations of CD-SAXS for logic applications have utilized large synchrotron facilities'.

claim: IRDS: current X-ray sources lack the brilliance for high-throughput in-line CD-SAXS on logic; future sources need at least 100x the brightness of current commercial lab sources (inverse-Compton sources named as one option)
unit: x brightness vs current commercial lab sources
document: IEEE International Roadmap for Devices and Systems (IRDS) 2024 Edition, Metrology chapter
quote: Current X-ray sources do not have a high enough X-ray brilliance to enable high throughput in-line metrology for logic application
note: Industry roadmap citing Kline et al., JM3 16(1) 014001 (2017) as ref [169] (that paper not retrieved). '100x' read across the page break: 'at least' on p.20, '100 [x] increases in brightness over current commercial lab sources' on p.21 (x is a symbol-font glyph). Same in 2022/2023 editions.

claim: IBM Research + Nova (JM3 2023): to apply X-ray scattering to patterned logic wafers, X-ray sources need more brightness, shorter acquisition and a smaller spot; shorter wavelengths (EUV, X-ray) are wanted for weak parameters and optically opaque materials
document: Schmidt D., Medikonda M., Rizzolo M., Silvestre C., Frougier J., Greene A., Breton M. (IBM Research) + Cepler A., Ofek J., Kaplan I., Koret R., Turovets I. (Nova), 'Spectral interferometry for fully integrated device metrology', J. Micro/Nanopattern. Mater. Metrol. 22(3) 031203 (2023), CC BY 4.0
quote: increased brightness of x-ray sources, decreased acquisition times, and decreased spot size allow for measurements on a sufficiently small area
note: Chipmaker research + Nova co-authored. Same page: 'shorter wavelengths toward EUV and x-rays would be desired for increased sensitivity to weak parameters of interest'. p.4: grazing-exit XRF and resonant soft X-ray scattering 'still far from being in-line capable'. p.2: OCD spot <40 x 40 µm2, desire to cut it at least 100x.

claim: imec + Nova (SPIE 2021): the GAA cavity-etch depth (inner-spacer CD) could then only be measured by slow cross-sectional electron microscopy; low-landing-energy SEM and AFM give little or no information on this buried CD
document: Bogdanowicz J. et al. (imec; TEL) incl. Hung J., Koret R. (Nova), 'Spectroscopy: a new route towards critical-dimension metrology of the cavity etch of nanosheet transistors', Proc. SPIE 11611, 116111Q (2021)
quote: this critical dimension (CD) can only be measured by time-consuming cross-sectional electron microscopy
note: Research body (imec) + vendor co-authored; OCD measured on a Nova T600 MMSR with Nova MARS software (p.5). PDF hosted by Nova.

claim: Same imec+Nova paper: OCD is very sensitive to cavity depth (fitted 13 and 28 nm vs nominal 15 and 30 nm; 9 parameters in <1 min) but responds to the whole geometry, so parameter correlations can give non-unique solutions; independent input from other techniques would help
document: Bogdanowicz J. et al. (imec; TEL) incl. Hung J., Koret R. (Nova), 'Spectroscopy: a new route towards critical-dimension metrology of the cavity etch of nanosheet transistors', Proc. SPIE 11611, 116111Q (2021)
quote: In some cases, correlations between these parameters may exist, which leads to non-unique solutions
note: Fitted values and '<1-min long non-contact measurement' on p.5; p.6 conclusion: 'OCD is very close to fulfilling the need for fast inline characterization of cavity depth'. Alternatives evaluated: EDX, Raman, XPS, SIMS (X-ray spectroscopies, not X-ray scattering).

claim: IBM Research + Nova (SPIE 2021): scatterometry is the only non-destructive in-line technique able to monitor sheet-specific SiGe indents on fully integrated GAA wafers at relevant pitches; desired accuracy <1 nm
document: Schmidt D., Durfee C., Pancharatnam S., Medikonda M., Greene A., Frougier J. (IBM Research) + Cepler A., Belkin G., Shafir D., Koret R., Shtainman R., Turovets I., Wolfling S. (Nova), 'OCD enhanced: implementation and validation of spectral interferometry for nanosheet inner spacer indentation', Proc. SPIE 11611, 116111U (2021)
quote: Scatterometry is currently the only available non-destructive in-line technique capable of sheet-specific monitoring of fully integrated wafers at relevant fin and gate pitches
note: Chipmaker research + vendor co-authored. p.2: 'Ideally, a metrology accuracy of <1 nm is desired'; OCD, XRF and 'maybe Raman' named as the only suitable in-line techniques for fully integrated samples. 'in-line' is hyphenated across a line break in the PDF text.

claim: Same paper: many floating parameters in fully integrated GAA models risk accuracy loss from parameter correlation because the etched SiGe volume is tiny; adding spectral-interferometry channels raised OCD-vs-STEM R2 for average indent from 0.8 to 0.9
document: Schmidt D., Durfee C., Pancharatnam S., Medikonda M., Greene A., Frougier J. (IBM Research) + Cepler A., Belkin G., Shafir D., Koret R., Shtainman R., Turovets I., Wolfling S. (Nova), 'OCD enhanced: implementation and validation of spectral interferometry for nanosheet inner spacer indentation', Proc. SPIE 11611, 116111U (2021)
quote: adding SI channels improves the correlation to STEM from R2 = 0.8 with MMSR channels only to the depicted R2 = 0.9
note: p.8 also: 'there is a risk that the model accuracy lacks due to parameter correlations, especially since the etched SiGe volume is very small'; 'a machine learning solution utilizing XRF as a reference was developed'. p.9: HRXRD-derived 'sheet factor' used to correct sheet-specific OCD results; p.10: 'maybe additional reference metrology using x-ray reflectometry'. Spectral interferometry is Nova's technique.

claim: IBM Research + Nova (IEEE TSM 2022): earlier work found preliminary CD-SAXS data on nanowire test structures sensitive to SiGe indent; the paper notes prior studies used short-loop test structures without the full device stack, and that the indent changes only ~1% of unit-cell volume
document: Schmidt D., Durfee C., Pancharatnam S., Frougier J., Breton M., Greene A. (IBM Research) + Cepler A., Klare M., Koret R., Turovets I. (Nova), 'Development of SiGe indentation process control for gate-all-around FET technology enablement', IEEE Trans. Semicond. Manuf. 35, 412 (2022); author version hosted by Nova
quote: angle x-ray scattering (CDSAXS) data indicate good sensitivity
note: Two-column PDF: quote is one text line. CD-SAXS work cited = Korde et al., Proc. SPIE 11325, 113250W (2020), with NIST co-authors (abstract on the 11325 volume page). p.1: 'within a unit cell is only around 1 %'. p.2: electron-excitation methods hard to use on full stacks (gate stack >100 nm).

claim: Same TSM paper: in-line LE-XRF gives Ge volume loss but no depth information, so sheet-specific indent reference data on full device stacks come only from TEM; authors want more non-destructive reference data
document: Schmidt D., Durfee C., Pancharatnam S., Frougier J., Breton M., Greene A. (IBM Research) + Cepler A., Klare M., Koret R., Turovets I. (Nova), 'Development of SiGe indentation process control for gate-all-around FET technology enablement', IEEE Trans. Semicond. Manuf. 35, 412 (2022); author version hosted by Nova
quote: XRF data lacks depth information
note: p.6 conclusion line: 'sheet-specific indent metrology, there is a desire for additional' [non-destructive reference data points]. Sheet-specific OCD vs TEM: middle/top sheets R2 > 0.92, bottom sheet lower (p.5).

claim: imec + Nova (SPIE 2025, CFET): at the middle-dielectric-isolation SiGe2 removal step, simulated sensitivity of classical OCD models falls as the SiGe residue shrinks, so ML is to be applied for residue measurement
document: Kwon H. et al. (imec) + Hung J., Urbanowicz A.M., Urenski R., Turovets I., Ger A. (Nova), 'Critical in-line OCD metrology for CFET manufacturing', Proc. SPIE 13426, 1342606 (2025)
quote: However, the sensitivity of classical OCD models decreases with the amount of remaining material
note: Research body (imec) + vendor co-authored; article number from Turovets 2026 ref [23]. p.3: for <10 nm superlattice layers 'quantum confinement effects significantly alter optical properties'.

claim: Same CFET paper: OCD vs TEM on 3 DoE wafers gave R2 0.85 (nanosheet top CD), 0.92 (bottom CD) and 0.99 (NS height); superlattice layers 0.87-0.92 in a 3 nm DoE; inner-spacer lateral recess 0.95
unit: R2 vs TEM (NS TCD / BCD / height)
document: Kwon H. et al. (imec) + Hung J., Urbanowicz A.M., Urenski R., Turovets I., Ger A. (Nova), 'Critical in-line OCD metrology for CFET manufacturing', Proc. SPIE 13426, 1342606 (2025)
quote: The R2 of 0.85, 0.92, and 0.99 for TCD, BCD, and NS height
note: Superlattice R2 0.90/0.92/0.87 on p.3; inner-spacer R2 0.95 on p.8. Shows the in-line role OCD keeps in a CFET pilot line; research + vendor co-authored.

claim: SPIE 2025 paper on in-line X-ray for CFET: XRD and XRR measure each SiGe/Si layer thickness and composition; in-line GI-SAXS gives width, height and inner-spacer cavity depth but needs deeper probing and a smaller beam footprint before it can serve CFET
document: Bogdanowicz J., Mingardi A., Brissonneau V. et al., 'Inline x-ray metrology for complementary field-effect transistors (CFET)', Proc. SPIE 13426, 134261G (2025) - abstract on SPIE proceedings volume page
quote: provides independent information about width, height and inner spacer cavity depth but would necessitate deeper probing depths and smaller beam footprint to enable CFET metrology
note: Abstract only; affiliations not shown on the volume page (first author is imec-affiliated in the 2021 paper, TH-024). Abstract suggests incident energies lower than Cu K-alpha. DOI 10.1117/12.3050810.

claim: SPIE 2026 CFET paper: TEM and OCD face throughput, scalability or sensitivity limits for recessed SiGe structures; micro-spot XRF tracked lateral recess with R2 ~0.996 to SEM/TEM and a ~1.4 nm 3-sigma calibration-limited floor across 495 dies per wafer
document: Kim J., Bogdanowicz J., Mingardi A. et al., 'Nanometer-scale SiGe lateral recess metrology in CFET structures using micro-spot x-ray fluorescence', Proc. SPIE 13981, 139810Z (2026) - abstract on SPIE proceedings volume page
quote: TEM and OCD provide valuable insight but face limitations in throughput, scalability, or sensitivity for recessed structures
note: Abstract only; affiliations not shown. X-ray here is fluorescence (volume/composition), not scattering. DOI 10.1117/12.3087689.

claim: SPIE 2025 GAA test-structure paper: hybrid metrology fed HRXRD layer thicknesses into an OCD model of an 8-layer superlattice nanowire test structure and cross-checked cavity etch with XRF Ge volume, reaching sub-nm agreement with STEM
document: Pasikatan E., Antonelli G.A., Keller N. et al., 'Hybrid metrology for non-destructive lateral cavity etch measurements of 8-superlattice layer nanowire test structures (NWTS) using optical MMSE, XRD and XRR', Proc. SPIE 13426, 134260Y (2025) - abstract on SPIE proceedings volume page
quote: Sub-nanometer matching to STEM was achieved with the nondestructive hybrid XRD/OCD and XRF feed forward method
note: Abstract only; affiliations not shown (Antonelli and Keller are also authors of the mid-IR paper TH-006). Test structures, not product wafers. DOI 10.1117/12.3052209.

claim: Nova review: after optical/e-beam/probe hybrids, hybrid metrology was extended to X-ray tools; its Table 2 (SPIE hybrid papers 2011-2016) lists 2013 '+ CD SAXS' on 14 nm Si lines, 2014 XRD hybrid, 2015 XRF/XPS hybrid, 2016 XPS on pattern
document: Turovets I. (Nova), 'The art of holistic metrology (in memory of Alok Vaid)', Proc. SPIE 13981, 1398104 (2026); manuscript posted by Nova
quote: the approach was extended to X-ray tools
note: Vendor-authored review. Table 2 read from the rendered page image (not in the text layer); the table cites an SPIE short course (ref [13]), not the original papers, so the 2013 CD-SAXS hybrid paper itself was not retrieved.

claim: Same Nova review: hybrid-metrology evaluations succeeded but wide use was limited by cost of ownership (extra toolsets and servers; every site measured at least twice); AI-enabled hybrids are presented as the cheaper route
document: Turovets I. (Nova), 'The art of holistic metrology (in memory of Alok Vaid)', Proc. SPIE 13981, 1398104 (2026); manuscript posted by Nova
quote: a widespread implementation of Hybrid metrology during these years was limited because of the cost (of ownership)
note: Vendor-authored. p.9 also: 'each measurement location is always measured at least twice by hybrid metrology tools'.

claim: IBM + Nova (SPIE 2019): hybrid metrology combining scatterometry (optical CD) with low-energy XRF plus ML quantified voids in BEOL Cu lines, for which no quantitative in-line method existed
document: Kong D. et al. (IBM) + Cepler A., Sendelbach M., Emans S., Isbester P., Shah K., Wolfling S., Ger A. (Nova), 'Machine learning and hybrid metrology using scatterometry and LE-XRF to detect voids in copper lines', Proc. SPIE 10959, 109590A (2019)
quote: by combining scatterometry (also referred to as Optical Critical Dimension or Optical CD) and low-energy x-ray fluorescence (LE-XRF)
